The path consists of three distinct points connected in sequence: M 55.58,17.52 → L 53.95,26.14 → L 47.22,29.95 → M 47.22,29.95 → L 48.21,22.28 → L 55.58,17.52.  
This creates two separate line segments from the first M command and then a new M command starts another path from (47.22,29.95) back to (55.58,17.52) via (48.21,22.28).  
The first part: (55.58,17.52) → (53.95,26.14) → (47.22,29.95) is two line segments.  
The second part: (47.22,29.95) → (48.21,22.28) → (55.58,17.52) is two more line segments.  
But the last point (55.58,17.52) is the starting point of the first segment, so the overall figure is a closed shape with vertices:  
(55.58,17.52), (53.95,26.14), (47.22,29.95), (48.21,22.28), and back to (55.58,17.52).  
That’s 4 distinct vertices: (55.58,17.52), (53.95,26.14), (47.22,29.95), (48.21,22.28).  
A 4-sided polygon is a quadrilateral, but the options don’t have “quadrilateral” — only “kite” is a possible specific type.

Also, diagonals? Not needed, but two distinct pairs of adjacent equal sides → kite.  

Final answer: (D)
